prompt.text:
Create ONE NEW independent native transparent NW running sprite of the CALLIGRAPHER BOY. Image1 (the boy) supplies identity, anatomy, outfit, head size and rear-left three-quarter NW camera, NOT a static pose to retain. Image2 (the archer girl) supplies the actual RUNNING BODY POSE: reproduce its anatomical near/far thigh overlap, flexion of each knee and ankle, forefoot/heel contact versus flight, and counter-swing rhythm using the BOY'S short proportions. Do not reuse a previous wrong pose just because it was in image1. Image3 is approved painterly/material style only. NW travel points diagonally away toward upper-left. Both boots' long axes follow upper-left NW with continuous knees/ankles, no external toe yaw and no mirrored flip. Draw distinct left and right legs from their actual hip joints following image2; baggy black short pants remain, not bare girl's legs. Preserve boy identity: brown compact topknot and taiji hairpiece, teal ribbons, charcoal black/gold cloud-pattern robe with ivory lining, teal belt and ORIGINAL decorations, gold-trim black boots. Anatomical LEFT arm holds a blank paper scroll with exactly TWO tiny pale-cyan ink spirits; anatomical RIGHT arm grips a large black/gold calligraphy brush, one teal tassel visibly chained to its gold BUTT end. Keep hands connected through the correct left/right shoulder and elbow, not merely screen-side prop swapping. Allow naturally bent elbows and forward/back arm motion; no stiff horizontal T arms. Never copy archer's face, long hair, green/white outfit, skirt, bow, quiver, arrows or bare legs. Single whole boy framed like 17 NW sprites, natural small body bounce, consistent head size/camera, no arbitrary image translation or ground snapping. Full square transparent RGBA canvas natively at least1024; aim1254. No text, no drawn ground/outline markers, no shadow disc, no frame sheet.
Extra anatomy constraints: Pants fully cover the legs down to boot cuffs, NO exposed skin above either boot. The visible NEAR LEFT shoulder must lead to the hand holding the SCROLL on the near/left side; the FAR RIGHT shoulder leads to BRUSH hand on far/right side. Do not exchange props. A forward right brush arm can be flexed/foreshortened with the fist higher near the far shoulder/head edge, not a big sleeve growing out of near left shoulder. Keep those identities, use elbow flexion and shoulder depth for motion.
REQUIRED PHASE: Far RIGHT mid-stance. Right foot remains on ground beneath body on far side. Near LEFT thigh crosses visibly in FRONT of far thigh as left knee begins to drive forward; left foot is folded/higher, no left ground support. Clearly use image2's near thigh occluding far leg. Near left scroll arm slightly forward, far right brush elbow recovering/back, proper shoulder identity.
